newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on stable peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on stable peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed unchanged at 23.50 percent on Monday after what traders said was a quiet session due to the peso remaining stable.
"A very stable foreign exchange market helped, besides which many preferred to await the outcome of Tuesday's primary auction," a trader said.

Money market analysts said primary rates had limited scope for further falls and bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) could well gain 25 basis points at the central bank auction on Tuesday.
Some traders, however, did not rule out the prospect of a fall in primary rates.
"In theory, and in line with secondary levels, primary short-term rates ought to increase, but term paper is still in demand, so 28-day rates could go down some more," a trader said.

Banco de Mexico assigned 28-day Cetes at 22.98 percent last week. Secondary 28-day Cetes rates closed down 25 basis points at 23.00 percent on Monday. The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.5 of a centavo firmer at 7.7980/7.8030 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 75 basis points at 25.50 percent on what traders said was late speculative buying.
Banco de Mexico drained liquidity of 1.726 billion pesos during the session through three auctions to sell paper.
Liquidity of 326 million pesos is scheduled to return to the market on Tuesday from previous secondary auctions and will be augmented by government spending of some three billion pesos, traders said.
